summary: Phase 4 Slice H (policy_acks + training + training_completions dual-write Mongo + Supabase Postgres) verified GREEN end-to-end. Backend pytest: 41/41 PASS in test_iteration17_phase4h_policies_training_dualwrite.py. (1) POST /api/policies/acknowledge as caregiver creates exactly one row in BOTH DBs for (policy_id, user_id=389b257d...); body returns policy_id+user_id+acknowledged_at; the PG row has matching policy_id+user_id::uuid; Mongo find_one returns same. (2) Re-posting the SAME policy is idempotent in BOTH stores — PG count stays 1 (ON CONFLICT (policy_id, user_id) DO UPDATE), Mongo count stays 1 (update_one upsert). (3) GET /api/policies/acknowledgments as caregiver returns ONLY user_id=CAREGIVER_UUID (server forces target=current.id; passing ?user_id=ADMIN_UUID is silently overridden — caregiver CANNOT peek). As admin without filter returns full list (>=1); with ?user_id=CAREGIVER_UUID returns only that user's acks (read source: Postgres). (4) DELETE /api/policies/acknowledge/{policy_id} removes the row from BOTH DBs (PG count -> 0, Mongo count -> 0) scoped to current.id only. (5) POST /api/policies/acknowledge with non-existent policy_id 00000000-... returns 404 (verified in db.documents.find_one before insert). (6) POST /api/training (admin) without file_base64: Mongo + PG rows created; PG storage_path IS NULL, title/description/required match. (7) POST /api/training WITH file_base64 (24-byte mp4 stub, mime=video/mp4) uploads to Supabase Storage bucket 'documents' under sub-prefix 'documents/<tid>.mp4'; PG row's storage_path = 'documents/<tid>.mp4' (contains training id); blob is verifiable via service-role list at prefix='documents'. (8) GET /api/training returns the merged list from Postgres for BOTH admin and caregiver — all created TIDs are in the list. (9) POST /api/training/{tid}/complete as caregiver creates a completion in BOTH DBs; re-completing the SAME (training, caregiver) pair returns the SAME completion id (PG: ON CONFLICT (training_id, caregiver_id) DO NOTHING -> Mongo find_one returns existing -> server returns TrainingCompletion(**existing) with original id; PG count stays 1, Mongo count stays 1). (10) GET /api/training/completions as caregiver returns ONLY caregiver_id=CAREGIVER_UUID; passing ?caregiver_id=ADMIN_UUID is overridden. Admin can filter via ?caregiver_id. Source: Postgres. (11) DELETE /api/training/{tid} (admin) — training row removed from BOTH; training_completions cascaded out of BOTH (PG via ON DELETE CASCADE on training_id_fkey; Mongo via explicit db.training_completions.delete_many({'training_id': tid})). (12) Phase 4 A–G regression GREEN under BOTH legacy HS256 (Admin@123) and Supabase ES256 (AdminPassword123!) JWTs across 10 endpoints (auth/me, caregivers, clients, assignments, documents, shifts, chat/threads, onboarding?caregiver_id=<demo>, policies/acknowledgments, training) — 20 parametrised tests all pass. (13) Final parity restored EXACTLY to baseline after cleanup: PG policy_acks=2 == Mongo policy_acks=2; PG training=0 == Mongo training=0; PG training_completions=0 == Mongo training_completions=0. Cleanup deletes tracked _training_ids + _storage_paths from PG (cascades completions), Mongo (training + training_completions), and Supabase Storage. (14) Frontend regression (Expo web, mobile 390x844): Supabase mode login (admin@healthguard.com / AdminPassword123!) -> Dashboard renders Audit Readiness 51%, 1 Client, 12 Caregivers, 50 Documents, 0 Trainings. Policies tab (admin) shows '2/20 acknowledgments' and 20 policy rows with Read buttons including '01 - Code of Conduct - Acknowledged 6/22/2026, 4:04:55 AM' (the existing baseline ack). Caregiver login (caregiver@healthguard.com / Caregiver123!) -> Policies tab shows '0/20 acknowledgments' for Sarah Johnson (baseline policy_acks=2 are both admin self-acks, not caregiver). Training Library route renders 'No training modules / Check back soon' (matches baseline training=0). No red-screen ReferenceError/TypeError anywhere. Smoke script /app/scripts/_smoke_slice_h.py PASSES against the live backend (full PG+Mongo flow). No Expo deprecated packages introduced.
action_items: (Optional) supa_data.upsert_training_completion uses 'on conflict (training_id, caregiver_id) do nothing'. That's correct for idempotency but the completed_at timestamp is NEVER updated even if a caller re-completes with a fresh value. The server-side path matches this — the existing-record branch in server.py:1200-1207 returns the existing Mongo doc unchanged. Consistent. No change required for Slice H, but if a future business rule needs 'last completed wins' the ON CONFLICT clause must change to DO UPDATE SET completed_at=excluded.completed_at.

(Optional) server.py:1167-1178 create_training writes Mongo first then PG via supa_data.upsert_training and supa_data.upload_document_blob_sync. If the Mongo insert succeeds but the Storage upload fails, supa_data._safe swallows the error and the client still gets 200. Same pattern as Slice C documents — acceptable until Slice J makes PG authoritative.

(Optional) server.py:1198-1212 complete_training reads existing from MONGO not PG. If Mongo training_completions drifts away from PG (e.g., stale Mongo row missing from PG), the heal call on line 1206 (supa_data.upsert_training_completion(existing)) catches it. This is the documented dual-write self-heal. Good.

(Optional) server.py:1034 acknowledge_policy still reads the policy doc from Mongo (db.documents.find_one({id, category:policy})). Since documents are dual-written (Slice C), this is safe — but when Mongo decommission begins (Slice J) this needs to switch to a PG lookup. The Slice H smoke test depends on Mongo having the policy doc.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:1028-1054 acknowledge_policy — Mongo update_one(upsert=True) + supa_data.upsert_policy_ack(ack) with ON CONFLICT (policy_id, user_id). Both verified idempotent by re-posting. The ack dict reuses the same id field across upserts (always a new uuid4), which is fine for PG (the id column isn't part of the conflict target) but means the PK 'id' on a re-ack actually CHANGES — see policy_acks.id::text returned changes between calls. Functionally OK since lookups are by (policy_id, user_id), but worth knowing.

server.py:1016-1025 list_acknowledgments — `target = current.id if current.role == 'caregiver' else user_id` correctly forces caregivers to only see their own. Verified by passing ?user_id=ADMIN_UUID as caregiver — server returns only caregiver's rows.

server.py:1057-1066 un_acknowledge_policy — scoped to current.id in BOTH stores. A caregiver can't delete another user's ack (no admin override path either — admin would need to call a separate endpoint or this should expose ?user_id; not in this slice's scope).

server.py:1165-1179 create_training — fb = t_dict.pop('file_base64', None) BEFORE upsert_training, so file_base64 never reaches PG (PG schema has no such column — correct). storage_path is set only when fb is truthy. Verified: PG storage_path IS NULL when no file, and 'documents/<tid>.<ext>' when file_base64 is present.

server.py:1189-1195 delete_training — Mongo delete_one(training) + delete_many(training_completions WHERE training_id) + supa_data.delete_training(tid). PG ON DELETE CASCADE on training_completions.training_id_fkey handles the PG side. Verified: completion row gone in BOTH after parent delete.

supa_data.upsert_policy_ack line 975 — `on conflict (policy_id, user_id) do update set user_name, policy_title, acknowledged_at = excluded.X` — id is NOT in the update clause so re-acks keep the original PG id. (Note: Mongo update_one with $set:ack DOES overwrite Mongo's id field — so PG id and Mongo id will diverge on every re-ack until next delete. Not a functional bug since neither id is used as a join key, but worth flagging.)
supa_data.upsert_training line 1026 — `on conflict (id) do update set ...` covers re-upserts of the same training (e.g., from healing flows). Good.

supa_data.upsert_training_completion line 1068 — `on conflict (training_id, caregiver_id) do nothing` is correct for idempotency: re-completing keeps the original PG row untouched and the server returns Mongo's existing row, which after self-heal upsert matches PG.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase 4 Slice H is GREEN. All policy_ack + training endpoints are dual-write: POST /policies/acknowledge writes Mongo update_one(upsert) then PG ON CONFLICT(policy_id,user_id) DO UPDATE via supa_data.upsert_policy_ack; DELETE /policies/acknowledge/{policy_id} scoped to current.id in BOTH; GET /policies/acknowledgments reads from PG with server-forced user_id=current.id for caregivers. POST /training writes Mongo insert_one then strips file_base64 and (if present) uploads to Supabase Storage as 'documents/<id>.<ext>' before PG upsert; storage_path persists ONLY in PG (Mongo keeps file_base64). POST /training/{tid}/complete uses Mongo find-then-return for the existing-completion branch (heals to PG via upsert_training_completion), and Mongo insert+PG upsert for the new-completion branch (PG uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING — re-complete returns SAME id from Mongo). DELETE /training/{tid} relies on PG ON DELETE CASCADE for completions (training_completions.training_id_fkey REFERENCES training(id) ON DELETE CASCADE) and explicit db.training_completions.delete_many in Mongo. Slice H's smoke test (/app/scripts/_smoke_slice_h.py) passes and the regression test (test_iteration17_phase4h_policies_training_dualwrite.py) covers 41 cases. Reusable fixtures: legacy_admin_token, supabase_admin_token, legacy_caregiver_token, policy_id (resolves first 'category=policy' doc), HA/HCG/HSUPA headers. The cleanup tracker uses module-scope autouse fixture so adding more tests to this file requires only appending to _training_ids / _storage_paths lists. Next slice per /app/scripts/ pattern is likely Slice I or J (Mongo decommission of the policy doc lookup in acknowledge_policy + the find-then-return in complete_training).
rca_of_issue: One minor test-script issue discovered and fixed during test development: the Supabase Storage verification in TestTrainingNoFile.test_create_training_with_file_uploads_to_storage was calling sb.storage.from_(bucket).list() with no prefix, which returns the top-level entries of the bucket (just the 'documents/' subfolder). Since storage_path is 'documents/<id>.mp4' (a file INSIDE the 'documents' subfolder of bucket 'documents'), the assertion needs `.list('documents')` to enumerate files at that prefix. Fix: split storage_path on '/' and pass the prefix to .list(). After fix: 41/41 pass. NO backend changes were required — Slice H backend is fully functional as designed.
